plain.text: At that time the whole world had one language. People settled in a plain in Shinar and said, "Come, let us build a city with a tower that reaches to the heavens, so that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the whole earth." The LORD came down to see the city and tower. He said that if as one people with one language they had begun to do this, nothing they planned would be impossible for them. So the LORD confused their language so they could not understand each other, and scattered them over the whole earth. They stopped building the city. That is why it was called Babel.
This is the family line of Shem, from Shem through Arphaxad, Shelah, Eber, Peleg, Reu, Serug and Nahor, to Terah, who had three sons: Abram, Nahor and Haran. The lifespans gradually become shorter.

Terah's son Haran had a son named Lot, and Haran died in Ur of the Chaldeans. Abram married Sarai, and Nahor married Milcah. Sarai was barren; she had no children. Terah took Abram, Sarai and his grandson Lot and set out from Ur for the land of Canaan. But when they reached Haran, they settled there, and Terah died in Haran.

summary.bigIdea: People try to make a name for themselves at Babel and are scattered; then the story narrows to one family, Abram and Sarai.
points: People build a tower to make a name for themselves.
God confuses their language and scatters them.
The family line leads to Abram, whose wife Sarai has no children.
summary.reflection: The builders of Babel wanted to "make a name for ourselves". Where do you see that desire in yourself or in our world?
